$comment: What a release of this workspace contains, and what it is built against.
Read by .github/workflows/ci.yml. Kept as an explicit file rather than
inferred from folder names, because the two decisions below are product
decisions and must be visible in a diff when they change.
$comment_platformImage: The ZuloOne image the bundles are exported BY, pinned rather than 'newest'.
A bundle is produced by importing this workspace into a running ZuloOne and
exporting each model back out, so the platform version is part of how the
artifact was made. Pinning it makes a rebuild of the same tag reproducible,
and records what a package was tested against — which matters once a model
declares a MinVersion on Core, since Core's version IS the platform's.
localhost:5000, NOT 10.10.0.210:5000, and the difference is not cosmetic.
The registry serves plain HTTP; Docker treats localhost as insecure by
default but refuses any other host without an insecure-registries entry.
The CI host has none, so the LAN address fails with 'server gave HTTP
response to HTTPS client'. This file is read only by CI, which runs on that
host, so the loopback name is the correct one here — tenants reach the same
registry by its LAN address because their host is configured for it.
$comment_exclude: Models that are NOT shipped to customers.
TestBench and TestBenchExt are fixtures for the in-app integration tests —
together the densest folders in the tree (169 files) and indistinguishable
from business models at the directory level. They must still be imported
during the build, because the tests that prove the workspace works live in
them; they simply must not be published.
Core is excluded for a different reason: it is not distributable at all.
docs/WORKSPACE.md §7.1 — Core is inseparable from the application, its
version IS the application version, and 'upgrade Core' means 'upgrade
ZuloOne'. A Core bundle would be a package that can never be installed.
